Results.ReviewText: I have not bought a bbq grill in many years, but my old one finally burned out.  I bought this grill primarily what I read about it in consumers report and what other customers have said about it.  I have had it about a month and used it quite a bit.  I really like it.  It cooks quite quickly.  There is a cooking guide card that came with it and I use it.  Once I have had it for a while I won't need it.  The grill ignitor is super, it is battery powered and not the clicker type.  The propane tank is inside the grill and it has a tank capacity indicator.  A very nice feature, BUT, it won't be easy to lift a full 5 gallon tank to hang it.  The two side shelves are very handy, and they fold down if you don't need them.  It seems to be everything I need in a grill.  After I use it more My rating might go up.
Results.Title: A good grill

Results.ReviewText: I bought this grill several years ago and have enjoyed using it since purchase.  However recently the plastic battery cap for the electric ignition broke in half rendering the electronic ignition useless.  I contacted Weber to try to order a replacement battery cap only to discover you must purchase the entire ignition module for $30+ in order to get a new plastic battery cap that costs all of a few cents to make and Weber could probably sell for $5.00.  Why is it that a part that is destined to fail (plastic + heat not a good combination) is not available for replacement as a reasonable price?  And if Weber does not provide an outlet for reviews on their customer service experience, then they should expect them on the product reviews.
Results.Title: NIce grill but not satisfied with Weber's support

I wouldn't recommend buying direct, I'd go through Lowes or another big-box store with more control over their delivery.

ClientResponses.Response:
Thank you for your feedback. We are so sorry to hear your grill is sputtering and going out. We are happy to help. 
  
It sounds like your grill may be in a safety mode known as “bypass." What’s happening is that the regulator thinks there’s a gas leak, so it reduces the pressure. Follow these instructions to reset the bypass safety mode. This is also the way you would want to start your grill each and every time.
 
1. Open the lid
2. Make sure all knobs are in the off position (including side burner if applicable)
3. Turn your LP tank on all the way
4. Wait 30-60 seconds
5. Turn the first burner to start/high (first position to the left)
6. Hit your igniter
7. Turn on all remaining burners
8. Close the lid to preheat to 500-550°F

Our Support team is reaching out to follow up. Please look for our outreach soon. Thank you!
ClientResponses.Name: Consumer Care

Results.ReviewText: We moved to a new house. My previous Weber grill was connected to the natural gas line. At this new house, I wanted the flexibility to move the grill around my back deck so I purchased a propane version. The previous natural gas version had a perfect steady even flame  to cook with when it was turned to its lowest temperature. When turning the temp to the lowest flame setting on this new propane version, the flame sputters and often goes out. I have to  turn the temp up to half to keep a low flame burning. Perhaps it is bad propane, is that possible?
Results.Title: Sputtering flame at lowest temperatute setting
